rules.rationale: Many heteroatoms give strong H-bond and dipole interactions that stabilize the aqueous phase.
Pure hydrocarbon character lacks polar contacts, so hydration is entropically and enthalpically disfavored.
Short SMILES track small polar solutes with favorable exposure of hydrogen-bonding groups to water.
Longer scaffolds add hydrophobic surface and conformational cost that weaken net hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Heteroatom density drives hydration free energy through hydrogen bonding and polarity; it may fail when intramolecular hydrogen bonding shields polar groups.

rules.rationale: Heavily ringed solutes are rigid and hydrophobic, giving poor cavity formation in water.
Acyclic polar chains hydrate readily because they can adopt conformations that expose donor and acceptor groups.
Non-aromatic solutes often carry saturated polar groups better hydrated than flat aromatic surfaces.
Branching buries polar functionality and reduces solvent accessibility of heteroatom sites.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the source ring relation, betting that ring scaffolds fail to transfer and instead hinder hydration through hydrophobicity, which may fail for polar heterocycles.

lesson: Source ring and branching effects are chemically motivated but only weakly supported, so deploy the heteroatom-driven hydration prior that rests on direct polarity and hydrogen-bonding mechanisms.
revision_summary: Kept the heteroatom hydration mechanism as the deployed skill and inverted the uncertain source ring/structure relation into a counter-hypothesis for diversity.
